### 2026-10-13 – # Day 1: Learning Onshape and Building My First Track Part

**1h**

# Day 1: Learning Onshape and Building My First Track Part

Today, I made my first part of the marble run. I started by learning how to use Onshape through its tutorial. At first, I didn't even know how I was supposed to log my hours, so I searched around the site until I found the tutorial. Before starting, I also set up Lapse so I could record my work.

At first, Onshape was very confusing because there were so many different tools to learn and I wasn't sure what to do. It didn't get much easier as I continued. Every time I thought I had figured something out, a new problem came along.

For example, when I tried to change the measurements of my square sketch, I accidentally deleted the plane and had to restart. When I tried using the Sweep tool for the first time, I kept selecting the wrong line, which made the result look strange or prevented it from changing at all.

Despite these problems, I managed to finish the first part of my marble run.

When it was time to download my work, I couldn't figure out how to do it. I had to search three different times: first, to learn how to download a file; second, to find out how to download the specific editable file I needed; and third, to figure out which settings to use.

Finally, I uploaded my files to GitHub before going to bed.

Tomorrow, I'll either make a funnel or add more straight and curved sections to the track.

**TL;DR:** Learned the basics of Onshape, overcame several modelling and exporting problems, and completed the first part of my marble run.

### 2026-10-13 – # Day 2: Made a Track and Funnel

**2h**

# Day 2: Made a Track and Funnel

Today, I made the first real section of track that a marble can roll along for a while. I designed it like a snake, with about three curves. I also made a funnel by following the tutorial.

As I continued working, I got the hang of Onshape and was able to make the track much more easily, although I still ran into a few problems. The trickiest part was figuring out a good design. Since I will eventually need to tilt the track downwards, I made a simple design that leads into the funnel.

While making the track, I ran into a few small problems. The first was with the Sweep tool. I accidentally made the track go up and down instead of from left to right, but I noticed the mistake quickly and corrected it. I also made some of the lines too close together, so I had to adjust the spacing multiple times because some sections were touching at the ends.

The biggest problem happened while creating the funnel. I kept making mistakes with the line creation tool by attaching lines to the wrong places and trimming the wrong parts. Specifically, I repeatedly attached the line for the edge to the inside of the square. This made trimming difficult and left a gap in the bottom part of the funnel. As a result, I had to restart or go back several steps multiple times.

Despite these difficulties, I finished the top layer of my track and created the funnel. I'm getting more comfortable with Onshape, and I now have a better idea of how to use the tools to build more complicated shapes.

**TL;DR:** Built the top section of my marble run with three curves and created a funnel, while learning to use the Sweep and line creation tools more effectively.
